approach: Root cause: the baseline keeps one pass/fail bit per check name. `Baseline::failed_before` matches by name and `verify::is_pre_existing` uses it, so a check failing on the base excuses every failure in that check, including a new, different failing test. Fix it at that comparison. (1) Add `failed_tests: Vec<String>` (serde default, skipped when empty) to `CheckRun`; `run_check` makes both baseline and candidate runs, so one field and one parser serve both. (2) For a plain `cargo test` Test check, `run_check` inserts `--no-fail-fast` after `test` so every binary runs; the recorded `command` stays as configured, and a failed run that got the flag says so in its `note`. (3) `failed_test_names(output)` parses cargo output section by section (one section per `Running`/`Doc-tests` line). It lists the indented `failures:` names qualified by binary, and adds the marker `<binary> (did not finish)` for any section with no `test result:` line (crash, abort, stack overflow, process::exit) or whose failed count differs from the names listed. Names are recorded only when the process exited with a code and the command is plain `cargo test` without `--fail-fast`; each name goes through the redactor. Anything else records an empty list. (4) `is_pre_existing`: if both sides have names, the check is pre-existing only when every candidate name (marker included) is in the base's names; otherwise the name-level rule stays. (5) `judge` adds one Minor, informational finding for a blocking check with names, splitting newly failing from already failing on the base; the existing `check X failed` reason is unchanged, so a failure counts once. Scope stated honestly: this covers case (a), a different test failing inside a check that already failed on the base. Case (b), a clash with a concurrent change, is not separated: the baseline is run on the job's fixed base, and rebasing or merging concurrent changes is out of scope. CHANGELOG and the design note say so, and (b) is an open question.

decisions.choice: Record failing test names as an optional `CheckRun.failed_tests`, filled in `run_check`, and keep the compile-forced one-line literal edits outside the listed deliverables (answers findings 1-8).
decisions.reason: `run_check` produces the baseline runs (`baseline_runs`) and the candidate runs, so one field and one parser give both sides the same shape. Candidate runs travel as `Vec<CheckRun>` through run/mod.rs, `mark_pre_existing`, `held_for_timeout` and `judge`. A new field forces `failed_tests: Vec::new()` in every struct literal the compiler reports; these are logic-free and the compiler checks them. I re-read the literals: routing.rs:214 uses `..skipped_run(...)` and needs no edit (finding 12), so the outside-deliverable edits are run/mod.rs:1293, routing.rs:451, status.rs:2826, run/send_back.rs:237, run/tests.rs:1504, introspect.rs:1728, reading.rs:4222 and crates/athena-cli/tests/status_durations.rs:12. The producer edits only literals the compiler reports.

rejected.option: Carry candidate names beside `Vec<CheckRun>` in a new struct, to avoid the literal edits
rejected.why: Changes the signatures of `mark_pre_existing`, `held_for_timeout`, `judge` and the run/mod.rs plumbing: a far larger and riskier edit than eight one-line field additions.
The tail is cut to 4096 bytes, so a long failure list loses names.
Overloads prose that other code matches on (`timed_out` reads the note).

decisions.choice: Make the name list complete in two layers: `--no-fail-fast` for plain `cargo test`, and a per-section completeness check in the parser that emits a `<binary> (did not finish)` marker (answers finding 9).
decisions.reason: By default cargo stops after the first failing binary, so later binaries' failures never appear. With `--no-fail-fast` every binary runs, but a binary that crashes prints no `failures:` list and no `test result:` line, so the list would still be a subset of the base (base {A X}, candidate {A X} plus crashed B gives {A X} and wrongly passes). The marker counts as new unless the base has the same marker, so the crash blocks. A section whose `test result: ... N failed` count differs from the listed names also gets the marker, so a truncated list cannot excuse a failure. Output with no `Running` sections yields an empty list and the name-level fallback.

rejected.option: Record no names when any binary looks incomplete
rejected.why: Falls back to the name-level rule, which excuses the new crash: the very masking being fixed.
Fragile wording match; the flag removes the case.

decisions.choice: Keep `CheckRun.command` as configured, and when Athena inserted `--no-fail-fast` into a failed run, append "ran with --no-fail-fast added to the configured command" to its `note` (answers finding 11). Document the same on the field and in the design note.
decisions.reason: The verifier matches commands against `CheckRun.command` (`judge` builds `ran` from it), so changing the string would break the `cargo test --locked` match. The note makes the difference visible to a later reader. It is added only to failed runs, so passing runs keep `note: None` (tests at checks.rs:651 and 654 rely on that) and `timed_out` is unaffected (it matches a different substring and requires no exit code).

rejected.why: The record would show a command that did not run.

decisions.choice: Fall back to the name-level rule when either side has no names. When both have names, a failing check is pre-existing only if every candidate name is in the base's names.
decisions.reason: fmt, clippy, build errors, timeouts, CI-reused results (`runs_from_record`) and old records behave as today; only runs with complete per-test evidence on both sides are tightened.

rejected.option: Treat a candidate failure with no names as new when the base had names
rejected.why: Changes `held_for_timeout` (it calls `is_pre_existing`) and build-error handling; beyond one focused change. Left as an open question.

decisions.choice: Qualify each name with its test binary as `<binary> <test>`, taken from the `(path)` in the `Running` line with the `-<hash>` suffix stripped; doc tests as `doc-tests <crate> <test>`.
decisions.reason: The same test name can exist in several crates, and the lib unit binary and the doc-tests share a crate name; bare names could excuse a new failure.

decisions.choice: Redact each name with `ctx.redactor.redact` before storing it; compare the redacted names on both sides.
decisions.reason: The field is written into Baseline and verdict records and needs the same handling as `output_tail`; both sides use the same function, so the comparison stays consistent.

decisions.choice: The split is one Minor Athena finding added in `judge` for a blocking check that has names; the `check X failed` reason remains the only thing that fails the verdict.
decisions.reason: The check already fails the verdict, so the finding is informational and must not count the same failure twice. send_back.rs does not read finding severities. A verify.rs test pins one reason, one Minor finding and verdict Fail.

rejected.why: A second blocking item for one failure.
A partly overlapping check is not marked pre-existing, so its note is not where the verdict is explained.

decisions.choice: State in the change description, CHANGELOG and design note that this change covers case (a) only; case (b) (a clash with a concurrent config/test change) is listed as an open question (answers finding 10).
decisions.reason: The baseline runs on the job's fixed base, so a failure that comes only from a concurrent change merged later is not in it. Separating that needs a rebase or merge check, which the brief puts out of scope. The entry must not overclaim.

rejected.why: Untrue; no code here compares against a moved base.

risks.risk: `CheckRun` has `deny_unknown_fields`; records with names do not parse on an older binary.
risks.mitigation: `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]`: records without names serialise as before. The old-shape parse test and the round-trip tests cover it.

risks.risk: Several CheckRun literals across the workspace (eight outside the deliverables) must gain the field; a miss breaks the build.
risks.mitigation: `cargo clippy --all-targets` compiles the tests and names any miss. The edits are one-line and logic-free.

risks.risk: The `failures:` format varies: the first `failures:` block is the stdout sections, and each binary and the doc-tests print their own list; stdout and stderr share one file, so section order could differ from the expectation.
risks.mitigation: Read only a `failures:` line whose next line is not blank; qualify by the section's binary; a section with a mismatched count or no result line gets the marker, which errs toward blocking, never toward excusing. Fixtures are literal text in cargo's exact format from a real local run.

risks.risk: A crashed or aborted binary leaves no list, so a new failure could be excused (finding 9).
risks.mitigation: The per-section completeness check emits `<binary> (did not finish)`, which counts as new unless the base has the same marker. Parser and verify tests cover it.

risks.risk: `--no-fail-fast` makes a failing test check run all binaries, so a failing run takes longer and the deadline may be hit more often.
risks.mitigation: Only failing runs get longer; passing runs are unchanged. A timeout records no names and keeps the name-level rule. The flag applies to baseline and candidate alike.

risks.risk: A flaky test failing on both sides is excused; a differently named flaky test now blocks.
risks.mitigation: Intended tightening with names on both sides; tests pin both directions.

risks.risk: The new finding could be counted twice.
risks.mitigation: Minor severity; a verify.rs test pins one reason and one finding; send_back.rs does not read finding severities.

risks.risk: The CHANGELOG could overclaim the fix by implying case (b) is handled.
risks.mitigation: The entry and the design note state the (a)-only scope; (b) is an open question.

risks.risk: The fake `cargo` script test could be flaky (exec of a just-written file).
risks.mitigation: Write and chmod it before the check starts, in a per-test tempdir; the pure `cargo_test_args` test covers flag logic without a process.

risks.risk: Refusal-corpus rule: the parser reads cargo output, not requests or readings.
risks.mitigation: Not applicable: the change adds no refusal or matching rule over requests or readings, so crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs is not touched and no case ids are cited. The parser has its own unit tests.

open_questions: Case (b), a failure caused by a clash with a concurrent config or test change, is not separated: the baseline runs on the job's fixed base. Separating it needs a check against a moved base (rebase or merge), which the brief puts out of scope.

When the base failed with test names and the candidate's check fails with none (build error, timeout, kill), the plan keeps the name-level rule, which still excuses it. A stricter rule would change `held_for_timeout` and is left out.
A base that failed with no names (build error) excuses a candidate that now has test failures, as today. Tightening that is a separate change.
A repo whose test check is not plain `cargo test` (wrapper script, nextest, `cargo +toolchain test`) records no names and keeps the name-level rule.
